questions.stem: Which description of the plot for the course to steer is correct?
options: Draw the track and the current vector from the start; from the end of the current vector swing an arc of the ship's speed to cut the track; join the end of the current vector to that point
Draw the current vector from the destination and swing an arc of the current's rate
Draw the ship's speed from the start and the current from the destination
Draw the track, add the compass error, and read the course
questions.explanation: The ship's own velocity plus the current's velocity must add up to a velocity along the track. The arc finds the ship's velocity vector, and its direction is the course to steer.

questions.stem: Track 090 degrees, speed 8 knots, current setting 040 degrees at 2 knots. What is the course to steer?
questions.explanation: The current sets partly northward of the track, so the bow goes south of it. Sine of the correction = 2 x sin 50 degrees / 8 = 0.19, so 11 degrees: 090 + 11 = 101. 079 puts the bow on the wrong side.

questions.stem: For the same problem (track 090, 8 knots, current 040 at 2 knots), what is the speed made good?
questions.explanation: Speed made good = 8 x cos 11 degrees + 2 x cos 50 degrees = 7.85 + 1.29 = 9.1 knots. The current has a fair component of about 1.3 knots along the track.

questions.stem: The course to steer is 342 degrees true. The compass error is 14 degrees E. What compass course is given to the helm?
questions.explanation: True to compass: subtract easterly error, 342 - 14 = 328. 356 adds it, and 342 forgets the conversion.

questions.stem: The wanted track is 095 degrees true, the ship's speed is 12 knots, and the current sets 170 degrees at 2.5 knots. What is the course to steer?
questions.explanation: The set is on the right of the track (170 is south of 095), so the bow is turned to the left. Sine of the correction = 2.5 x sin 75 degrees / 12 = 0.20, so 11.6 degrees: 095 - 11.6 = 083. 107 puts the bow on the down-current side.

questions.stem: Track 000 degrees, speed 8 knots, current setting 180 degrees at 2 knots. What are the course to steer and the speed made good?
questions.explanation: The current is dead against the track, so there is no cross-track part and no correction is needed; the current simply subtracts 2 knots.

questions.stem: A ship steers 270 degrees at 6 knots. The current sets 180 degrees at 1.5 knots. What are the track and speed made good?
questions.explanation: West 6 nm and south 1.5 nm: track = 270 - arctan(1.5 / 6) = 270 - 14 = 256. Speed made good = square root of (6 squared + 1.5 squared) = 6.2 knots. 284 puts the track on the wrong side.

questions.stem: A track is 18.3 nm long and the speed made good is 9.14 knots. What is the time on passage?
questions.explanation: Time = distance / speed made good = 18.3 / 9.14 = 2.0 h. Using the ship's speed through the water of 8 knots gives 2.3 hours, which is the wrong speed.

questions.stem: A boat doing 4 knots must cross a current whose cross-track part is 5 knots. What is the result?
options: She must steer directly into the current
She can hold the track at a speed made good of 1 knot
No course can hold the track, because the cross-track current exceeds her speed
She steers the track and makes good 4 knots
questions.explanation: The arc of radius equal to the ship's speed never reaches the track. She can only be carried down-current, turn back, or wait for the current to ease.

questions.stem: To which side of the track does the bow point to counter a current?
options: To the up-current side, the side the water is coming from
To the side of the destination's bearing from the current
questions.explanation: The bow is pointed up-current of the track, by an angle that cancels the cross-track part of the current.

questions.stem: Which formula checks the correction angle for a course to steer?
options: Sine of the correction angle = ship's speed x rate / sine of the track
Tangent of the correction angle = rate / ship's speed, whatever the set
Sine of the correction angle = rate x sine of the angle between the set and the track, divided by the ship's speed
questions.explanation: The cross-track part of the current is rate x sin(angle between set and track). The bow must give an equal and opposite cross-track part of the ship's speed, ship's speed x sin(correction angle). Setting them equal gives the formula.
